facts.text: Pocomoke City, dubbed "the friendliest town on the Eastern Shore", was renamed in 1878 after the river's name meaning "black water".
The historic MarVa Theater, a 1927 Art Deco auditorium, now hosts live performances and is being restored as a regional performing‑arts center.
The Sturgis One Room School Museum, moved downtown, preserves African‑American education history and is part of the town’s cultural heritage.
Pocomoke City’s downtown Historic District, listed on the National Register, showcases Victorian, Colonial Revival, and Beaux‑Arts architecture from 1830‑1946.
The town grew around a railroad line built in the 1880s, part of the Pennsylvania Railroad, linking Wilmington to Cape Charles.
Pocomoke City hosts the Delmarva Discovery Museum, an interactive exhibit focused on local ecology and history.
